# Loading models

## Overview

The `ems_model()` function loads the model and its closure, conducts pre-deployment checks, determines temporal dynamics, and allows for the loading of aggregated coefficient data.
The output of this function is a tibble with attributes containing the parsed model input and is a required input to the `"model"` argument of the [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd) function.

```r
ems_model(model_file, closure_file, omit = NULL, backsolve = NULL,
          auto_omit = FALSE, ignore_condense = FALSE, ...)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `model_file` | Character | File name in working directory or path to a `.tab` file |
| `closure_file` | Character | File name in working directory or path to a `.cls` closure file |
| `omit` | Character vector or `NULL` | Exogenous, unshocked variables to omit from the condensed system |
| `backsolve` | Character vector or `NULL` | Endogenous variables to substitute out by backsolving |
| `auto_omit` | Logical | Omit every unshocked, wholly exogenous variable at deploy time |
| `ignore_condense` | Logical | Ignore `Omit`/`Substitute`/`Backsolve` statements found in the model file |
| `...` | Named arguments | Coefficient value injections (numeric, data frame, or CSV path) |

Both `model_file` and `closure_file` are required arguments.

## The model file {#tab_files}

Model input in `teems` is currently limited to Tablo (`.tab`) files.
Vetted models and their closures are available at [teems-models](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models) and can also be accessed via the [`ems_example()`](example.qmd) function.

| Model | Files | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| GTAPv6 | `GTAPv6.tab`, `GTAPv6.cls` | GTAP version 6.2 format |
| GTAPv7 | `GTAPv7.tab`, `GTAPv7.cls` | GTAP version 7.0 format |
| GTAP-RE | `GTAP-RE.tab`, `GTAP-RE.cls` | GTAP rational expectations (version 2, on the v7.1 core) |


Users may load their own models by providing a path to a Tablo file and closure:
```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = "path/to/custom_model.tab",
  closure_file = "path/to/custom_model.cls"
)
```

We recommend that users seeking to load custom models first review the formatting of the vetted models at [teems-models](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models) in order to make any necessary modifications for use within the `teems` software ecosystem.
In some cases it may be easiest to use existing compatible models as a starting point for modifications.
Although the [teems-solver](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-solver) does not support all current GEMPack declarations, there is usually a workaround.
Running a `diff` on the original GTAP models and those in [teems-models](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models) is a good starting point for understanding potential incompatibilities.

## Closure selection
Standard model-specific closures are available within the model repository: [teems-models](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models).
The general format consists of an `exogenous` block listing all (`\n` delimited) exogenous variables, followed by `;`, `rest endogenous`, and `;` to mark the end:

```
exogenous
pop
aoreg("row")
qe(ENDWC,REG,INITIME)
txs(MARG,"row",REG,FWDTIME)
...
;
rest endogenous
;
```

Each entry is either a full variable name (`pop`), an entry with specific set elements (`aoreg("row")`), an entry with subsets (`qe(ENDWC,REG,INITIME)`) or a mixed entry (`txs(MARG,"chn",REG,FWDTIME)`).

## Incompatible features

The [teems-solver](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-solver) was originally designed to emulate GEMPack, and we have no intention of attempting to reproduce the very thorough [GEMPack documentation](https://www.copsmodels.com/gpmanual.htm) on the Tablo scripting language and underlying solution software.
*Most* Tablo model files (`.tab`) that work with GEMPack will also work with the [teems-solver](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-solver) with some minor modifications.
There are however a range of newer GEMPack features that are not compatible and are not likely to be incorporated.
Fortunately there are workarounds for the vast majority as described below.

Considerable efforts have been made to correctly parse Tablo files, but it is likely that custom Tablo files will need to be modified.
If you find an incompatibility not listed here and feel that it should be addressed, please feel free to contact us with your model file.
Some of the more frequent incompatibilities and workarounds are listed below.

### Supported Tablo statements

The parser recognizes the following Tablo statements: `File`, `Coefficient`, `Read`, `Update`, `Set`, `Subset`, `Formula`, `Assertion`, `Variable`, `Equation`, `Write`, and `Zerodivide`.
Statements not in this list are either unsupported (e.g., `Omit`, raising an error) or ignored (`Postsim`, raising a warning).

### Set and subset declarations

**Set expressions** follow the GEMPACK specification (manual 10.1.1.1): the operators `UNION`, `INTERSECT`, `+`, `-` and `\` may be combined over declared sets and quoted single elements, with parentheses for grouping, evaluated left to right.
```
Set A123 = A1 + A2 + A3;
Set B = (C - D) INTERSECT E;
Set COSTS = "IntDom" + "IntImp" + ENDW + "PTAX";
```
As in GEMPACK, `+` requires disjoint operands and `-` may only remove elements that are present; both are validated at deployment.
Subset relations are implied where the manual defines them (all-`UNION`/`+` expressions, all-`INTERSECT` expressions, and trailing top-level `UNION`/`INTERSECT` terms); declare a `Subset` statement explicitly in other cases.
Set names must not contain the substrings `union` or `intersect`.

**Set equality** follows the GEMPACK specification (manual 10.1.2.1): a new set may be declared equal to a previously defined set, which also implies the two `Subset` statements in both directions.
```
Set A # example set A # maximum size 5 read elements from file GTAPSETS header "H2";
Set B # example set B # = A;
```
The intertemporal conversion forms `Set (Intertemporal) B = A;` and `Set (Non_Intertemporal) B = A;` (manual 13.3.1) are not supported: neither set in an equality statement may be intertemporal.

**Conditional set builders** (GEMPACK manual 10.1.2) select the elements of a set from data at run time:
```
Set ENDWM # mobile endowments # = (all,e,ENDW: ENDOWFLAG(e,"mobile") ne 0);
Set ENDWS_COMM # sluggish endowments # = (all,i,ENDW_COMM: SLUG(i) > 0);
Set BIGB = (all,b,BLOC: sum{r,REG: REGTOBLOC(r) = b, RGW(r)} > 7.5);
```
The condition is a single comparison (`= <> < > <= >=` or `eq ne lt gt le ge`) of a coefficient reference against a constant; the reference carries the loop index once, plus quoted elements for its other dimensions.
The condition coefficient is either `Read` from an input file or an *indicator* assigned constants only, such as GTAP-AEZ's `UNITDCROP(a) = 0.0 + IF[a in DCROPACTS, 1.0]` or GTAP-E's `UNITDCOAL(c) = 0.0 + IF[c = "coa", 1.0]`: the selection is evaluated ahead of formulas, so any other formula-computed operand cannot drive it (a named error).
teems evaluates the same condition from the deployed (aggregated) data at `ems_deploy()` so closure/shock validation and system sizing see the elements, and keeps the statement verbatim for the solver, which re-evaluates it; an empty selection is an error, as in GEMPACK.
The mapping-conditional sum form (third example; GTAP-E's and GTAP-AEZ's `UNITD*` flags) needs the sum to range over the mapping's domain set and the builder over its codomain set, with the mapping read `(by_elements)`; the mapping values are composed under the active aggregation exactly as the deployed mapping header is (see the GTAP-AEZ `DACTS`/`MACTS` sets, [data loading](data_load.qmd)).
The flag-header approach of the upstream GTAP models (`ENDOWFLAG` read from `EFLG`, `SLUG`) is not supported through the R package: those headers are dropped from the data (`full_exclude` option) and a set built from them raises a named error. Declare such sets explicitly instead
```
Set ENDWM # mobile endowment # (capital, unsklab, sklab);
```
(the solver on its own accepts the flag form).

**Set products** (`Set UACT = UNITA x ACTS;`, GEMPACK manual 10.1.6) are supported: elements are named `a_b` with the first factor varying fastest, and when a pair of names would exceed GEMPACK's 12-character element limit the compromise names of manual 11.7.11 are produced (`c2food_row`).
The `$POS` intrinsic (manual 11.5.6), `Mapping (project)` from a set product (10.13.2) and mappings assigned by `Formula` statements (10.13.1) are supported as well, so the upstream GTAPv7 PostSim welfare-report block loads as written.

**Capital goods.** The `CGDS` sector in v6.2 format models is renamed to `cgds` by default due to R `data.table` C-locale sorting and preference for all set elements to be lowercase.

### Formulas and Equations

**IF conditionals** (GEMPACK manual 11.4.5--11.4.7) are supported in Formula and Equation statements when each `IF[condition, expression]` enters additively at the top level of an expression, as in
```
Formula (all,c,COMM)(all,r,REG)
    VCB(c,r) = VDB(c,r) + sum{d,REG, VXSB(c,r,d)} + IF[c in MARG, VST(c,r)];
Equation E_qca # supply of commodities by act. a # (all,c,COMM)(all,a,ACTS)(all,r,REG)
    qca(c,a,r) = IF[MAKES(c,a,r) gt 0, qo(a,r) - ETRAQ(a,r) * [ps(c,a,r) - po(a,r)]];
```
Three condition forms are supported: set membership (`c in MARG`), index--element equality (`d = "domestic"`), and a comparison of two coefficient expressions (`MAKES(c,a,r) gt 0`, `THETAi(j,r)*YDONOFF(j,r) <= 0`, `VTRPROV(r) > VT`, with `eq`/`ne`/`gt`/`lt`/`ge`/`le` or the equivalent symbols); conditions cannot reference variables.
At model load these statements are rewritten into equivalent unconditional statements (narrowed-domain formulas, split equations, or synthesized 0/1 indicator coefficients named `IFC*`, with helper sets named `IFS*` and, for expression conditions, helper coefficients named `IFX*` that inherit the host formula's `(initial)`/`(always)` qualifier); the helper coefficients appear in solve outputs like any other coefficient.
A membership condition whose set is the quantifier's set or a declared subset of it narrows to that set directly (no `IFS*` set is synthesized).
An `IF` whose expression itself carries `IF` terms is rewritten recursively, so GTAP-AEZ's land equations (a membership branch on the endowment holding a membership branch on the activity holding a data comparison, `E_qfe`; four activity-class branches inside an endowment branch, `E_qes2`) and its calibration formulas load as written.
A Formula whose right-hand side references its own target (`ESUBVA(a,r) = IF[a in NLANDACTS, ESUBVA(a,r)] + IF[a in LANDACTS, ...]`) reads the pre-assignment values through a synthesized copy coefficient named `IFT*`.
Several membership or element conditions may appear in one Equation when they condition the same index (they partition the equation's domain, e.g. GTAPv7's `IF[d="domestic", ...] + IF[d="imported", ...]`); the parts must not overlap.
Not supported: compound conditions (`AND`/`OR`/`NOT`), `IF` nested inside sums or products, and membership conditions on different indices at one level of an Equation.

### Source-file conventions

The following spellings, all accepted by GEMPACK, are normalised silently: keywords glued to their first bracket (`Coefficient(all,r,REG)`, `Formula(Initial)`), block comments `![[! ... !]]!`, empty statements (`;;`), empty labels (`# #`), Latin-1 or CRLF files and a UTF-8 byte-order mark, and several statements on one line.
`Read (IfHeaderExists)` is supported: an absent header is skipped by the solver and the coefficient keeps its formula or default value, and `ems_deploy()` does not require such headers in the loaded data.
Label text outside any statement (a `# label #` placed after the terminating `;`) is a named error, since GEMPACK would read it as the start of the next statement.

## Condensation {#condensation}

Condensation reduces the size of the system passed to the solver by removing variables, following GEMPACK semantics (GEMPACK manual, sections 10.16 and 14.1).
Two actions are available; both leave the model's economics unchanged.

### Variable omission {#var_omit}

Variables specified with `omit` are set to zero in the model file and removed from the closure.
Omitted variables must be exogenous in the closure and must not be shocked; an error is raised otherwise, or if a variable designated for omission is not found in the model.

Standard v7.0 data format variable omissions (gtapv7.sti): `c("atall", "avaall", "tfe", "tfd", "tfm", "tgd", "tgm", "tpdall", "tpmall", "tid", "tim")`.
Standard v6.2 data format variable omissions: `c("atall", "tfd", "avaall", "tf", "tfm", "tgd", "tgm", "tpd", "tpm")`.

Nominating omissions by hand is optional: `auto_omit = TRUE` omits every variable that is exogenous in each of its elements and carries no shock.
Such a variable has a change of zero, so dropping it removes columns from the shock vector without altering the solved system --- the deployed system size is unchanged.
The set can only be established once swaps and shocks are known, so the work happens in [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd), which reports what it omitted.
Omitted variables are absent from solve outputs, and a variable referenced outside `Equation` and `Update` statements is left alone.

### Backsolving {#backsolve}

Variables specified with `backsolve` are substituted out of the system using a nominated defining equation: the equation is rearranged into the form `x = ...` and the resulting expression replaces every occurrence of `x` in all other equations.
The defining equation is retained in the deployed model together with a `Backsolve` statement, so the solver can recover the variable's values after each solution step --- backsolved variables remain available in solve outputs, unlike plain GEMPACK substitution (which `teems` deliberately does not implement).

Unnamed entries resolve their defining equation by the `E_<variable>` naming convention; named entries specify it explicitly:

```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAPv7[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAPv7[["closure_file"]],
  backsolve = c("pfd", "pfm", "qfe", ps = "E_ps")
)
```

Backsolved variables must be endogenous.
Each nomination is validated against the GEMPACK substitution requirements (GEMPACK manual, section 14.1.10): every occurrence of the variable in the nominated equation must have plain, distinct indices (no elements, no lead/lag offsets, no `SUM` indices) matching the equation's quantifiers exactly, ranging over the variable's full declared sets, and all occurrences must share one index pattern.
Violations abort with the failed requirement.
Because substitutions are applied in order, an earlier substitution can make a later nomination invalid (or valid); nominations are validated against the current, rewritten form of each equation.

When a rearrangement divides by a coefficient expression (e.g., `GDP(r,t) * qgdp(r,t) = ...`), the reciprocal is synthesized as a coefficient and a warning is issued: the expression must never be zero.
To control expression growth, `teems` synthesizes intermediate coefficients (named `CSUB*`) with defining formulas, mirroring GEMPACK's system-initiated coefficients; these appear in solve outputs like any other coefficient.

### When backsolving pays {#backsolve_when}

Substitution shrinks the system but densifies it: each eliminated variable's defining expression is spliced into every equation that referenced it.
That trade is worth taking under `matrix_method = "LU"` on static models, where the cost is dominated by the size of the single factorization.
It is counterproductive under the bordered methods (`"SBBD"`, `"DBBD"`, `"NDBBD"`), which exploit the block sparsity substitution destroys, and on intertemporal models generally.
[`ems_solve()`](solve.qmd) reports this when a condensed deployment meets a bordered method, and [`ems_probe()`](probe.qmd) settles it from the measured block structure --- a system with a usable partition belongs to a bordered method, one without is `"LU"`-bound.
Omission is unaffected: it removes exogenous columns and densifies nothing.

### In-TAB condensation statements

`Omit`, `Substitute`, and `Backsolve` statements inside the model file (GEMPACK manual, section 10.16) are honored:

```
Omit a1 a1oct a1mar ;
Substitute p1 using E_p1 ;
Backsolve p1lab using E_p1lab ;
```

All omissions execute first, then substitutes/backsolves in the order they appear, followed by any actions supplied through the `omit` and `backsolve` arguments.
`Substitute` statements are executed as backsolves (with a message), so the affected values stay available in outputs.
Set `ignore_condense = TRUE` to ignore in-TAB condensation statements entirely (the equivalent of GEMPACK's `ICT` option).

The vetted `GTAPv6.tab` and `GTAPv7.tab` carry the standard GTAP condensations (`gtap.sti`, `gtapv7.sti`) as in-TAB statements: the omissions listed above and 60 (v6.2) or 72 (v7.1) backsolves.
They therefore condense automatically when loaded; to shock one of the omitted variables (e.g. `atall`, `tfd`), or to solve the full system, load them with `ignore_condense = TRUE`.
A backsolve nominating an equation that the IF rewrite has split into per-element partitions (the v7.1 `CNTqfr`, `CNTqgr`, `CNTalleffr`, `CNTtechr` summaries) is skipped with a message and the variable stays in the solved system.

## Coefficient value injection {#coeff_inject}

The `...` argument in `ems_model()` allows users to assign aggregation-specific values to model coefficients.
This is used to inject modified values into existing coefficients as well as provide data to new coefficients.
All data inputted here must be model-aggregation specific and will not be subject to aggregation.
The left-hand side (name) must correspond to a coefficient (not header) declared within the model input.
Data frame and CSV inputs are validated against the set aggregations from [`ems_data()`](data_load.qmd).
Dimensions must match the aggregated resolution, not the original database resolution.
Three input types are supported, with model "Read" and "Formula" declarations modified accordingly:

### Uniform numeric value

A single numeric value can be assigned to a coefficient.
All set combinations for that coefficient will receive this uniform value.

```r
GTAP_RE <- ems_example("GTAP-RE")
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  KAPPA = 0.54321
)
```

Providing a numeric vector of length greater than 1 will raise an error.
Instead here use a data frame with the appropriate sets to assign multiple heterogeneous values to a coefficient.

### Data frame

A data frame (or data frame extension such as tibble or data.table) can be used to assign heterogeneous values across set combinations.
The data frame must contain columns for each set index using the model-specific naming convention (set name + variable index, e.g., `REGr`, `COMMc`, `ALLTIMEt`) and a `Value` column.

```r
# Heterogeneous values for SUBPAR coefficient (Read-type)
GTAP_RE <- ems_example("GTAP-RE")
COMMc <- c("crops", "food", "livestock", "mnfcs", "svces")
REGr <- c("usa", "chn", "row")
ALLTIMEt <- seq(0, 10)

SUBPAR <- expand.grid(
  COMMc = COMMc,
  REGr = REGr,
  ALLTIMEt = ALLTIMEt
)

SUBPAR$Value <- runif(nrow(SUBPAR))

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  SUBPAR = SUBPAR
)
```

This works for both `Read`-type and `Formula`-type coefficients:

```r
# Heterogeneous values for CPHI coefficient (Formula-type)
REGr <- c("usa", "chn", "row")
ALLTIMEt <- seq(0, 10)

CPHI <- expand.grid(
  REGr = REGr,
  ALLTIMEt = ALLTIMEt
)
CPHI$Value <- runif(nrow(CPHI))

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  CPHI = CPHI
)
```

### CSV file

A path to a CSV file can be used as an alternative to a data frame.
The CSV must follow the same structure: set index columns and a `Value` column.

```r
# Write coefficient data to CSV
write.csv(SUBPAR, "SUBPAR.csv", row.names = FALSE)

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  SUBPAR = "SUBPAR.csv"
)
```

### Combining injections

Multiple coefficient injections can be combined in a single call along with variable omissions:

```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  omit = c("atall", "avaall", "tfe", "tfm", "tgd", "tgm", "tid", "tim"),
  KAPPA = 0.03,
  SUBPAR = SUBPAR,
  CPHI = CPHI
)
```

If the coefficient name is not found in the model, an error is raised indicating that the aggregated data coefficient is not declared within the provided model input.

### Set naming convention

Set names follow a model-specific concatenation of the standard set name and the variable-specific index (e.g., `REGr`, `COMMc`, `ACTSa`).
See the [Loading and specifying sets](set_mappings.qmd) chapter for the full convention table.

## Intertemporal models {#intertemporal}

For intertemporal models, `ems_model()` determines temporal dynamics by detecting intertemporal sets in the Tablo file.
By default, the expected header in the GTAP-RE model is `"YEAR"`.
If a model uses a different header for timestep data, set it via [`ems_option_set()`](options.qmd):

```r
ems_option_set(timestep_header = "AYRS")
```

If the expected timestep header is not found in the model, an error will be raised with a suggestion to use [`ems_option_set()`](options.qmd) to configure a custom timestep header.
The same concept applies to the number of timesteps:

```r
ems_option_set(n_timestep_header = "NINTERVAL")
```

Default values for these settings (and others) may be obtained using:

```r
ems_option_get()
```

### Inter-period links and the netcut {#netcut}

The parallel matrix methods (`"SBBD"`, `"DBBD"`, `"NDBBD"`; see [Solving the model](solve.qmd)) order the linearized system into independent diagonal blocks plus a dense border containing the variables that couple time periods.
Every element of a variable referenced with a lead or lag (e.g. `kb(r,t+1)`) is placed in this border, so a lead or lag on a variable declared over large non-time sets inflates the border (the *netcut*) by the product of those set sizes and can eliminate the advantage of the parallel methods.

When a lead or lag reference fixes one or more dimensions to quoted elements (e.g. `qo("capital",r,t+1)`), `ems_model()` repairs the model automatically: it synthesizes a minimal proxy variable (`NCV1`, `NCV2`, ...) over the remaining dimensions, ties it to the element slice with a linking equation (`E_NCV1`, ...), and moves the lead or lag onto the proxy.
A message lists each synthesized proxy; the proxies and their linking equations appear in solve outputs like any other variable.

For references that run over full sets, no mechanical reduction is possible, so `ems_model()` instead warns when a variable declared over two or more non-time sets is referenced with a lead or lag.
The remedy is to link periods through a minimal intertemporal proxy declared over only the elements that genuinely cross periods:

``` default
Variable (all,r,REG)(all,t,ALLTIME)
    kb(r,t) # beginning-of-period capital stock #;
Equation E_kb
(all,r,REG)(all,t,ALLTIME)
    kb(r,t) = qo("capital",r,t);
```

with the lead placed on the proxy (`kb(r,t+1)`) rather than on `qo(COMM,REG,ALLTIME)`.
The shipped intertemporal models already follow this discipline.
